target_customer: Home gardeners buying indoor and outdoor gardening supplies, and independent garden shops selling to them
problem: Gardening supplies are sold by thousands of small shops with no good online marketplace, so home gardeners cannot easily find and buy what they need.
business_model: Marketplace with take rate on sales from garden shops

founders.name: Vera Kutsenko
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says she led mobile app teams at Uber. YC page adds that she is a certified personal trainer.

founders.name: Hayley Leibson
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in the April 2021 TechCrunch article; the YC page lists only Kutsenko.

competitors.name: Bloomscape
competitors.what: Direct to consumer online plant retailer
competitors.funding_then: 15M Series B in September 2020, after a 7.5M Series A

competitors.name: Sproutl
competitors.what: UK online marketplace for gardeners selling through independent garden centres
competitors.funding_then: about 9M dollars seed led by Index Ventures in July 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: A marketplace connecting shop inventory to buyers is standard e-commerce engineering, with the main difficulty in onboarding many small shops.

defensibility.rationale: Supply from thousands of independent shops could build marketplace liquidity, but nothing structurally blocked Amazon or plant retailers from the same shops.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes incumbent moves against Neverland.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in April 2021 described a pandemic gardening boom and cited Breck's sales data; the YC page sizes the market at 26 billion dollars and cites about 24,000 US shops.

branding.domain_note: Company site is enterneverland.com, an enter prefix, not neverland.com.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly literary name and a TechCrunch feature, but the name is shared with many companies and the company needed a prefixed domain.

outcome_analysis: Neverland was a Winter 2021 garden and lawn marketplace by two founders with Facebook, Uber and LunchClub backgrounds that raised 4.7 million dollars in a seed round announced in April 2021. YC marks it Inactive, but no shutdown notice, acquisition or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are assigned. Whether it wound down or pivoted is unconfirmed.
notes: The seed amount and investors come from TechCrunch, and the amount matches the CB Insights seed dated 5 March 2021; CB Insights totals 4.83M over 2 rounds and lists Kindred Ventures and Jack Chou, so a small earlier round may be missing. Round date is the TechCrunch announcement. enterneverland.com returned HTTP 503 on fetch. Sproutl source is dated about four months after the W21 batch. The link between the founders and Wordware appeared only as a search result title and was not verified.
